description: Which object a name points to. Compared with `is`; `id(obj)` is its CPython address-like number and should not be asserted.
Whether two objects have equivalent value. Compared with `==`, which calls `__eq__`.
A unique `object()` used as a marker value (for example 'no default given') so that `None` stays usable as real data.
The value `__eq__` and operator methods return to say 'I do not know this type'; Python then tries the other operand or falls back.
CPython reuses some small integers and strings. It is an implementation detail: never compare numbers or strings with `is`.
